text:
maya: quick heads-up — provisioning queue in eu-west spiked, ~12 nodes failing PXE after last BMC push. some come up with secure-boot toggled ON unexpectedly.
kevin: ugh. any pattern on hardware/vendor?
sasha: looks like mix of A100 racks and a couple T4 hosts. NIC link down/up flaps + autoneg negotiating to 100Mbps on a subset. reprovision time jumps from ~4m to ~18m.
dave: please paste the BMC push id + commit hash.
maya: push id = fw-roll-2026-03-15-4; commit = 5c3a9b2. infra-bot started rollout at 3923456600.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout started to eu-west (batch size 50). monitoring: https://redwood.internal/rollouts/fw-roll-2026-03-15-4
kevin: can you share a short snippet from journal or ipmitool output for one affected node?
sasha: pasted one below:
```
# ipmitool -I lanplus -H 10.2.15.23 -U admin -P **** sel elist
SEL Timestamp : 03/15/2026 10:22:13
SEL Type : System Event
SEL Data : BMC: NIC link down
SEL Data : NIC link up (100Mbps)
SEL Data : Secure Boot state changed: Enabled
```
kevin: that secure-boot flip is the smoking gun. vendor note said 'enable SB by default on specific SKUs' in release notes but we scoped to disabled.
maya: rollout config definitely set `secure_boot: false` in our pipeline. looks like BMC is asserting a flag during postflash.
elena: correlation: the nodes that flipped all went through the same OOB management controller firmware path that toggles platform policy during init. maybe a regression.
oncall-ryan: current impact to infra SLA? how many GPU slots are out of allocatable pool?
dave: counting — 12 nodes (48 GPUs) stuck in provisioning, 6 in staging canary that are fine. effective available capacity in eu-west down ~8%.
kevin: cost impact: containers queued -> fallback to US-west, extra cross-region egress + scheduling churn. estimate incremental spend ~+$1.6k/day if this persists.
sasha: immediate mitigation options: 1) pause rollout (stop further BMC flashes) 2) remote trigger policy rollback on affected BMCs 3) reimage nodes with local netboot bypass (manual) 4) route new jobs to other regions and spin up reserved capacity.
maya: i've paused the rollout pipeline: `ROLLBACK=true` set and aborting remaining batches. infra-bot confirmed stop at 3923456708.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout paused (reason: unexpected secure-boot toggles). active batches halted.
dave: great. for the 12 affected, can we attempt remote BMC-only rollback to previous image (fw-2026-02-28)? vendor exposes `bmc-revert` endpoint that we can script.
kevin: +1 on scripted revert. we should do a small canary 2 nodes first and validate NIC autoneg and secure boot state.
elena: i'll take canary nodes r1-03 and r1-07. doing `bmc-revert --image fw-2026-02-28 --host 10.2.15.23` now.
sasha: if revert fails, fallback is to force secure boot off via ipmi nvram flags and reprovision, but that leaves firmware newer and we should track vendor fix.
oncall-ryan: schedule note: if we need to mass rollback, we'll need a maintenance window to avoid affecting pipelines. Ops leaning towards incremental background reverts to avoid big downtime.
maya: also seeing a subset reporting PSU thermal throttle around the same time — could be coincidental but increases reprovision time. logs show repeated BMC reboots during flash window.
dave: vendors engaged (ticket #VND-4812). they asked for BMC log bundle (collected) and samples.
kevin: next steps: 1) complete 2-node canary revert (elena) 2) confirm secure-boot remains OFF and NIC autoneg stable (sasha) 3) run batch revert script in groups of 4, monitor reprovision latency 4) open temporary autoscale bump in eu-west to cover capacity shortfall (maya) 5) update runbook with vendor rollback steps (dave)
elena: canary revert succeeded on r1-03, r1-07. secure boot state now `Disabled` and link negotiated at 10Gbps. reprovision time back to ~5m.
sasha: running health check on the 10 remaining affected nodes now. will post failures.
maya: i've approved a temporary autoscale bump + reserved pool increase for eu-west until this is resolved. tickets: INF-8092 (capacity bump).
oncall-ryan: set alert to catch any nodes where `SecureBoot` transitions more than once in 15m.
dave: i'll draft rollback script: `./scripts/bmc_mass_revert --hosts ${HOSTLIST} --image fw-2026-02-28 --parallel 4` and a dry-run mode. will push PR to infra-playbooks.
kevin: good, also add gating check that `firmware.release_notes` not contain `enable-secboot-default` before future rollouts.
maya: vendor replied: "we see an edge-case where platform policy written to NVRAM flips SB when hardware revision X2 sees specific NIC EEPROM state during postflash". vendor working on a patched image.
sasha: long-term: update flash pipeline to include explicit nvram policy writes postflash and a CI step that boot-tests autoneg and secure-boot state.
elena: finishing remaining reverts now (starting batch). expecting ~30m to clear all 10.
kevin: thanks. once all reverts done, we should run a 24h canary and then coordinate with vendor to reattempt safe rollout. add hold until vendor provides fixed image + release notes.
maya: logging incident summary in postmortems channel after wrap.
kevin: nice job triaging everyone. :thumbsup:
